status_summary: On 2025-11-20 DOE released a new organization chart that lists the Office of Electricity and CESER as separate offices; a law-firm summary of the reorganization reports that the Office of Electricity moved under the Under Secretary of Energy. DOE's FY2027 budget justification, dated April 2026 per CRS, states that Grid Deployment Office activities were functionally realigned into the Office of Electricity in November 2025, and requests $203.5 million for the office, $56.3 million or 22 percent below the comparable FY2026 enacted level of $259.8 million that counts the realigned Grid Deployment activities; it cuts energy storage by 39 percent and requests no funding for the Distribution and Markets program. The justification does not mention combining the office with CESER, and the cuts depend on appropriations.

uncertainties: The budget document prints no date; the April 2026 date comes from a CRS report citing the DOE justifications. Its overview table prints a 28 percent decrease on the Electricity account row and 22 percent on the total row, both against the same $56.3 million change; the 22 percent figure matches the comparable FY2026 base of $259.8 million and is used here, while 28 percent appears to compare against a different base and is not adopted. The organization chart is a flattened list that shows no reporting lines, so the placement of the office under the Under Secretary of Energy rests on a law-firm summary and a trade article; the Grid Deployment Office realignment is confirmed by the budget justification. Overlaps c12-17 (which tracks the possible combination with CESER), c12-20 (internal regrouping) and c12-01 (Grid Deployment Office and applied programs); this record is limited to the Office of Electricity's applied programs and structure.
